mainTopic: Learning rules for all קרבנות from the list in the פסוק 'זאת התורה לעולה למנחה ולחטאת ולאשם ולמלואים ולזבח השלמים' (ויקרא 7:37)
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier question: two different תנאים learn the same rule (that only male כהנים eat the communal שלמים) from two different sources. Then the גמרא goes through the פסוק that lists the קרבנות (ויקרא 7:37) and shows how each name teaches a rule for all the others. From חטאת we learn that absorbed meat makes things holy. From אשם we learn that a שפיר and שליא are not holy, and the גמרא names two opinions this תנא must hold. From מלואים we learn that leftovers are burned, though never a living animal, and from שלמים we learn the laws of פיגול. Next comes a ברייתא in the name of רבי עקיבא, which learns the absorption rule from מנחה. The גמרא explains why the תורה had to write that rule for both מנחה and חטאת. רבי עקיבא's ברייתא then learns from חטאת that every קרבן comes from חולין, is offered by day, and is done with the right hand. רב חסדא gives the source for the חולין rule, and the גמרא shows that the daytime and right-hand rules were mentioned only in passing, or that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. The ברייתא ends with אשם, teaching that the bones of every listed קרבן are permitted. Finally, רבא begins a new teaching, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two תנאים, two sources for the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves why there seem to be two sources: each תנא uses a different one.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is one תנא who learns it from here, and there is another תנא who learns it from there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question about why the rule that only male כהנים eat the communal שלמים has two sources. It says each source belongs to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, it looked like one source would make the other one extra and unneeded. The answer is that there is no extra source here. One תנא learns the rule from the explicit example of the מנחה, and the other learns it from the wide reading of the פסוק about מנחה, חטאת and אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it / he learns it

phrases.english: There is one who derives it from here,
and there is one who derives it from there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous section of the daf about why two sources are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like one of the two sources was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source is needed, because each one belongs to a different תנא.

steps.title: Sin offering: absorbed meat makes things holy
steps.stepSummary: From the word חטאת in the list, all the listed קרבנות make a vessel holy through what it absorbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sin offering': just as a חטאת makes things holy through what is absorbed into them, so too all the קרבנות in the list make things holy through what is absorbed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going word by word through the list of קרבנות in the פסוק. The word חטאת teaches a rule that now applies to all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of making something holy through contact is written explicitly about the חטאת. Because the פסוק lists חטאת together with the other קרבנות, that rule is carried over to every קרבן in the list. So a vessel that absorbs meat from any of these קרבנות becomes holy.

phrases.english: "Sin offering": just as a sin offering sanctifies through what is absorbed,
so too all of them sanctify through what is absorbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new reading of the list of קרבנות in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every קרבן in the list makes things holy through absorbed meat, the same as a חטאת.

steps.title: Guilt offering: fetal sac and placenta are not holy
steps.stepSummary: From the word אשם, a שפיר or שליא found in any listed קרבן is not holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Guilt offering': just as in an אשם a fetal sac and placenta are not holy, so too in all the קרבנות a fetal sac and placenta are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the list, אשם. It learns a rule about a שפיר and a שליא found inside an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם is always a male animal, so it never has a שפיר or שליא inside it. The גמרא still uses the אשם as the model: just as nothing like that is holy in an אשם, it is not holy in any of the listed קרבנות either. This includes female animals, which can carry a שפיר and שליא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think an אשם had a שפיר that was not holy. An אשם is male and never has one at all. That is exactly why the next step has to explain how we can learn from it.

phrases.english: "Guilt offering": just as with a guilt offering
a fetal sac and a placenta are not sacred within it,
phrases.notes: An אשם is always male, so it can never contain these.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל אֵין שָׁפִיר וְשִׁלְיָא קָדוֹשׁ בּוֹ.
phrases.english: so too in all of them a fetal sac and a placenta are not sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אָשָׁם״ – מָה אָשָׁם אֵין שָׁפִיר וְשִׁלְיָא קָדוֹשׁ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next קרבן in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שפיר or שליא found inside any of the listed קרבנות is not holy.

steps.title: What this תנא must hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out two opinions this תנא must hold for the אשם derivation to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the offspring of קדשים become holy only once they are born, and that we may learn a case where something is possible from a case where it is impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the thinking behind the אשם derivation. It names two views this תנא must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, if a fetus were already holy inside its mother, a שפיר would surely be holy. So this תנא must hold that וולדות קדשים become holy only at birth. Second, an אשם can never have a שפיר, while other קרבנות can. So learning from the אשם means he holds דנין אפשר משאי אפשר.

keyTerms.meaning: At their coming into being (at birth)
We learn a possible case from an impossible case

steps.whyThisMatters: Both of these principles are argued about elsewhere in ש״ס. This step shows that the derivation from the פסוק matches only one side of each argument.

phrases.english: He holds: offspring of sacrificial animals
are sanctified only as they come into being,
and one derives the possible from the impossible.
phrases.notes: A female can have a שפיר, which is 'possible'; a male אשם cannot, which is 'impossible'.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: וַולְדוֹת קָדָשִׁים בַּהֲוָיָיתָן הֵן קְדוֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning that the אשם derivation depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This תנא holds that וולדות קדשים become holy at birth, and that דנין אפשר משאי אפשר.

steps.title: Inauguration offering: leftovers are burned, but not live animals
steps.stepSummary: From the word מלואים, leftovers of all listed קרבנות are burned, but a living animal never counts as a leftover.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Inauguration offering': just as the leftovers of the מלואים were burned, and no living animals were among the leftovers, so too for all the קרבנות: their leftovers are burned, and living animals are not counted among the leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the word מלואים in the list. It learns two rules from it for all the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the מלואים, leftover meat and bread were burned, but no living animal was ever burned as 'leftover'. So for every listed קרבן, leftovers get שריפה, but an extra living animal is not killed and burned. One example is a backup animal set aside in case the first was lost.
steps.whatToRemember: Each word in the list teaches a rule for all the קרבנות. חטאת teaches that absorbed meat makes things holy. אשם teaches that a שפיר or שליא is not holy. מלואים teaches that leftovers are burned, but never a living animal.

phrases.english: "Inauguration offering": just as with the inauguration offering
their leftovers are disposed of by burning,
and there are no living animals among their leftovers;
so too all of them: their leftovers are disposed of by burning,
and there are no living animals among their leftovers.
phrases.notes: For example, a backup animal that wasn't needed is not killed and burned as a 'leftover'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next קרבן in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftovers of all the listed קרבנות are burned, but a living animal is never treated as a leftover to be burned.

steps.title: From peace offerings: every listed offering follows the rules of פיגול
steps.stepSummary: From the word שלמים, every קרבן in the list can cause פיגול and can become פיגול, just like שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Peace offering": just as a peace offering has parts that can make it פיגול and parts that can become פיגול, so too all the listed offerings have parts that can make them פיגול and parts that can become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this reading of the list by learning one more law from the word שלמים in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With שלמים, a wrong intention during a key service (like the blood) can make the whole קרבן פיגול, and the meat then becomes פיגול. The ברייתא spreads this two-sided rule to every קרבן named in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They cause פיגול (they make the offering invalid through a wrong intention)
They become פיגול (they are made invalid)

steps.whatToRemember: This first reading learns a separate law from each name in the פסוק: חטאת, אשם, מלואים, and now שלמים, which teaches פיגול.

phrases.english: "Peace offering": just as peace offerings
cause פיגול and become פיגול,
phrases.notes: "Cause" means parts like the blood, where a wrong thought makes the offering פיגול. "Become" means parts like the meat, which then turn פיגול.

phrases.english: so too all of them cause פיגול and become פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same ברייתא, after מלואים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All קרבנות listed in the פסוק can cause פיגול and become פיגול, like שלמים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא: absorption learned from the meal offering
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא, in the name of רבי עקיבא, learns the law of בלוע from מנחה instead of from חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a ברייתא it was taught in the name of רבי עקיבא: "Meal offering": just as a meal offering makes holy whatever absorbs it, so too all the listed offerings make holy whatever absorbs them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that reads the same פסוק in a different way, starting with the word מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading (step 2), the law that a קרבן makes something holy through what it absorbs came from חטאת. רבי עקיבא's ברייתא takes this same law from מנחה, and it uses the word חטאת to teach other rules (step 9).

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things holy through what is absorbed into them

phrases.english: In a ברייתא it was taught
in the name of רבי עקיבא:
"Meal offering": just as a meal offering
makes holy through what is absorbed,
so too all of them make holy through what is absorbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that reads the same פסוק differently
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the law of בלוע for all listed קרבנות is learned from מנחה.

steps.title: Why the Torah wrote absorption for both the meal offering and the sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the law of בלוע had to be written for both מנחה and חטאת, because neither one could be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write this law for the meal offering, and it was necessary to write it for the sin offering. If the Torah had told us only about the meal offering, I would say that because it is soft it gets absorbed, but a sin offering does not. And if it had told us only about the sin offering, I would say that is because its fat seeps out, but a meal offering does not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why does the Torah write the law of absorbing for both מנחה and חטאת, when one should be enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one has its own reason to be absorbed: the מנחה is soft, and the חטאת meat is fatty and seeps out. So we could not copy the law from one to the other. Each needed its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeps out or drips (because of its fat)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רבי עקיבא. The גמרא is only explaining why the Torah wrote the same law in two places.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write meal offering,
and it was necessary to write sin offering.
For if it had taught us only meal offering,
I would say that since it is soft, it gets absorbed,
but a sin offering, I would say not;
and if it had taught us only sin offering,
I would say that is because it seeps out,
but a meal offering, I would say not;
so both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב מִנְחָה, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the Torah wrote בלוע for both מנחה and חטאת
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason, so neither can be learned from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One פסוק should be enough for the law of בלוע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one has a separate reason for being absorbed (soft vs. fatty), so both פסוקים are needed.

steps.title: From the sin offering: non-sacred animals, daytime, and the right hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא learns from חטאת that every listed קרבן comes only from חולין, is offered by day, and is done with the כהן's right hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Sin offering": just as a sin offering comes only from non-sacred property, is offered by day, and with the right hand, so too all the listed offerings come only from non-sacred property, are offered by day, and with the right hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי עקיבא continues and uses the word חטאת to teach three rules for all the listed קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this ברייתא already learned בלוע from מנחה, the word חטאת is now free to teach other rules. Whatever is true of a חטאת, being bought with חולין, done in the daytime, and done with the right hand, applies to all the others too.

phrases.english: "Sin offering": just as a sin offering
comes only from non-sacred property,
and by day, and with his right hand;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל אֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין,
phrases.english: so too all of them come only from non-sacred property,
and by day, and with his right hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״חַטָּאת״ – מָה חַטָּאת אֵינָהּ בָּאָה אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי עקיבא's ברייתא after the side explanation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All listed קרבנות come only from חולין, are offered by day, and are done with the right hand.

steps.title: How do we know a sin offering must come from non-sacred property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a חטאת itself must come only from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the sin offering itself, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where the basic rule about חטאת comes from. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learned all the other קרבנות from חטאת, but it never showed why a חטאת must come from חולין. Before the comparison can work, the original rule needs a source.

phrases.english: And sin offering, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the first rule only: that it must come from חולין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule the ברייתא relied on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that a חטאת comes only from חולין

steps.title: רב חסדא: "which is his" means from his own property
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from the words "אשר לו" that the חטאת must come from the owner's own property, not from community funds and not from מעשר money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The verse says, "And אהרן shall bring the bull of the sin offering which is his." This means from his own property, not from the community's and not from tithe money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by pointing to a פסוק about אהרן's חטאת on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "which is his" show that the animal must belong to him personally. That rules out the community's money and מעשר money, which is not fully his. So the חטאת must come from plain חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull of the sin offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns בלוע from מנחה, and learns חולין from חטאת. The ברייתא also lists daytime and right hand under חטאת, but the גמרא shows these are mentioned only in passing (כדי נסבה). The rule that a חטאת comes from חולין is based on "אשר לו".

phrases.english: רב חסדא said: The verse says:
"And Aaron shall bring the bull of the sin offering
which is his": from his own,
and not from what belongs to the community
and not from tithe.
phrases.notes: This means money of מעשר שני, which must be spent in ירושלים and is not fully his to use as he likes.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אשר לו" teaches that the animal must be from his own property: not community funds and not מעשר, meaning only חולין.

steps.title: Daytime is already learned from another verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why learn from חטאת that offerings are brought by day, when the פסוק 'ביום צותו' already teaches it?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'By day': this is already learned from the words 'on the day of His commanding'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one of the rules from step 9, that every listed קרבן is offered by day. It asks why we need חטאת to teach this, since another פסוק already says it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ביום צותו' (ויקרא 7:38) are understood to cover all קרבנות. If so, learning the daytime rule from חטאת seems unnecessary. The גמרא is asking why the ברייתא bothered.

keyTerms.meaning: by day; the rule that the עבודה is done in the daytime
it comes out from; it is learned from

phrases.english: 'By day':
phrases.notes: This refers back to the ברייתא's rule from step 9, that every listed קרבן is offered by day.

phrases.english: this is learned from 'on the day of His commanding'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 9 and questions one of its rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of חטאת as the source for the daytime rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A separate פסוק, 'ביום צותו', already teaches that all offerings are brought by day, so learning it from חטאת adds nothing.

steps.title: The ברייתא mentioned it only in passing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא really did not need חטאת for this rule. It just mentioned it along with the other rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cited it for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the daytime rule really comes from 'ביום צותו'. The ברייתא mentioned it with חטאת only because it was already listing the other rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not argue with the question. It accepts that the source for the daytime rule is somewhere else. The ברייתא's mention is just extra, not a true source.

keyTerms.meaning: he cited it for no reason; it was mentioned only in passing

phrases.english: It cited it for no reason.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point: the mention is extra and not a real source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that the daytime rule comes from חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real source is 'ביום צותו'. The ברייתא just listed it along with the other rules.

steps.title: The right-hand rule is already taught by ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: why learn the right-hand rule from חטאת, when ריש לקיש taught that wherever 'finger' or 'כהונה' is written, it means the right hand?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With his right hand': this is already learned from רבה בר בר חנה's teaching. For רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of ריש לקיש: any place where 'finger' or 'כהונה' is said, it means only the right hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about another rule from step 9, that the עבודה is done with the כהן's right hand. That rule seems to be already known from ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule is general: whenever the Torah says 'finger' or 'כהונה', the right hand is required. If so, the ברייתא does not seem to need חטאת for this.

keyTerms.meaning: priesthood; a פסוק that mentions the כהן

phrases.english: 'With his right hand':
this is learned from רבה בר בר חנה's teaching,
as רבה בר בר חנה said
that ריש לקיש said:
Any place where 'finger' or 'priesthood' is said,
phrases.notes: 'Priesthood' means a פסוק that says the כהן does the action.

phrases.english: it means only the right hand!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית – מִדְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 12, now aimed at the right-hand rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of חטאת as the source for the right-hand rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש's general rule already requires the right hand wherever 'finger' or 'כהונה' is written, so חטאת is not needed.

steps.title: Again, mentioned only in passing
steps.stepSummary: The same answer as before: the ברייתא mentioned the right-hand rule only in passing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cited it for no special reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 13. The right-hand rule really comes from ריש לקיש, and the ברייתא just mentioned it along with the other rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the גמרא accepts the question. The ברייתא's mention is extra, and the real source is ריש לקיש's general rule.

phrases.english: It cited it for no reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 the same way step 13 answered step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point: the mention is extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that the right-hand rule comes from חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real source is ריש לקיש. The ברייתא just listed it along with the other rules.

steps.title: Or: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ברייתא holds like רבי שמעון. By his view, 'כהונה' alone does not mean the right hand, so the listed offerings really do need חטאת as their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: he holds like רבי שמעון, who said: where 'finger' is written, 'כהונה' is not needed; where 'כהונה' is written, 'finger' is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer, one that makes the ברייתא's source really needed. The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds that 'כהונה' alone, without 'finger', does not require the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי שמעון's view, the word 'finger' alone is enough to require the right hand. The word 'כהונה' alone is not enough, and it needs 'finger' with it. Since the listed offerings do not mention a finger, the right-hand rule really does need to be learned from חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say; introduces a second answer

steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread רבי שמעון as saying 'finger' needs 'כהונה'. It is the other way around: 'finger' is enough alone, but 'כהונה' alone is not enough.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
he holds like רבי שמעון, who said:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of רבי עקיבא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: 'Finger' does not need 'priesthood',
phrases.notes: Where a פסוק says 'finger', that word alone is enough to require the right hand.

phrases.english: 'priesthood' needs 'finger'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 14, one that makes the ברייתא's source really needed instead of extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the ברייתא inside a specific opinion (רבי שמעון), which makes its source necessary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's rule seemed to make חטאת unnecessary as a source.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבי שמעון's view, 'כהונה' without 'finger' does not require the right hand. So the listed offerings need חטאת as the source.

steps.title: From אשם: the bones of every listed offering are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: just as the bones of an אשם are permitted for use, so are the bones of every listed קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אשם': just as the bones of an אשם are permitted, so too the bones of every listed offering are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting רבי עקיבא's ברייתא, now at its next word, 'אשם'. From the אשם it learns a rule for all the listed offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same method the ברייתא used with חטאת. One offering in the list teaches a rule that applies to all of them. Here the rule is that the bones have no holiness and may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: just as ... so too; a comparison formula

phrases.english: 'Guilt offering':
just as a guilt offering, its bones are permitted,
so too every one, its bones are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 9 and continues to its next item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the bones of an אשם are permitted for use, the bones of every listed קרבן are permitted too.

steps.title: רבא begins a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבא introduces a point he considers obvious. The details come in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me that...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new teaching from רבא. He starts by saying something is obvious to him, and the case itself comes right after this opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's list of rules is finished, and a new section begins here. When an אמורא says 'פשיטא לי,' he is marking one case as clear to him. Often this prepares a contrast with a case he is less sure about.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious to me. The speaker treats the next case as clear and needing no proof

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a full statement on its own. Don't look for a ruling yet; the obvious case is stated in the next words.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is obvious to me that

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא's rules end in step 17, this opens a new teaching from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא introduces a case he considers obvious. The content of that case follows in the next part of the text.
